{# auth-bar.html — the persistent lower bar ("dock"). CONTRACT (keep in sync across neohiro / frenzypenguin-media / openstageisland / transhumanists): 1. AI and Contact are ONE thing here. There is no separate Contact tab and no separate chat form. The only composer is the assistant ask bar that network-ux.js mounts (#ai-bar), which talks to the real Mouth endpoint via /.well-known/ask. The previous dock-local form POSTed to '/api/contact', which does not exist on GitHub Pages, so every message silently failed. 2. Login lives in the TOP bar (see nav.html). The dock only surfaces the signed-in state (Dashboard / avatar) and the sign-out control. 3. Selecting "Assistant" hands off to network-ux.js, which slides this dock down and slides the screenwide conversation sheet up behind it. The page behind stays scrollable and interactive. 4. THE RAIL IS THE PERSISTENT NAVBAR FOR THE MAIN PAGE. Its leftmost item is the AI-bar button (#ai-dock__tab--ai) — network-ux.js routes it to the mainframe bridge for an answer, and to the voicemail queue for triage that reaches godadmin. To its right, every top-level section of index.md appears as an in-page anchor, driven by the `main_sections` list in _config.yml so this template cannot drift from the page. Anchor targets are same-document on the home page; from any other page they become "/" + fragment, so the rail never links to a section that is not on the document it is rendered in. The remaining panels are kept because auth-bar.js wires them by id and the top-bar Login button calls AuthBar.selectTab('login'). #}
{# ── LEFT: the AI bar. Assistant answers via the mainframe bridge (/.well-known/ask) and escalates to voicemail triage (/.well-known/voicemail) that reaches godadmin. #} {# ── MIDDLE: every top-level section of the main page, as anchors. `on_home` is true only when the current document IS the main page, so the hrefs are bare fragments here and absolute everywhere else. There is deliberately NO hardcoded fallback list. This template is shared by four sites whose home pages carry different section ids, so a baked-in list would put pills in every site's bottom bar pointing at fragments that do not exist there — dead links are worse than no links. A site that does not declare `main_sections` gets a clean bar (AI bar + account); declare the list in _config.yml to switch the group on. #}
{# `sec_frag` arrives as "#home" (the config spells it as a fragment so it is unambiguous there). The href needs it verbatim; the data attribute needs the bare id, because that is what getElementById() takes. #} Home{# `sec_frag` arrives as "#home" (the config spells it as a fragment so it is unambiguous there).
